title: Building a visual system from the report's own data
subtitle: EBANX, 2026
description: A generative visual identity for EBANX's annual report, built in p5 as a 3D Perlin noise orbit where each circle is a country sized by the share of adults making or receiving digital payments.
solution: Gave a report about global payments an identity that was made from its own dataset, so the visual system and the findings stayed in sync. EBANX's in-house team then used the orbit for the launch assets.
focus: Handoff to a team that kept using it

title: Letting visitors see their own pose matched to strangers' museum photos
subtitle: The Social Museum | DAE, 2025
description: An installation and website about how people pose with artwork in 2,251 Instagram photos taken inside modern and contemporary art museums.
solution: Designed one experience across two touchpoints, a camera installation and a take-home website, so visitors grasped the research by standing in front of it. Their portrait lands on the site with everyone else captured that day. In collaboration with Kosara Keskinova.

title: Helping newsroom designers hit the brand palette without deciding color every time
subtitle: Folha de S.Paulo, 2022
description: Folha's palette was small enough that charts kept reaching outside it. I expanded it in keeping with the paper's visual identity, then defined which combinations to use and what each one means. The new palette replaced the old one across the newsroom.
solution: The old palette forced designers to invent color combinations on the spot, so charts drifted from their meaning. The expanded set gave each combination a job, and every pair was checked for accessibility.
focus: Expanding a palette within an existing identity

title: Rebuild a three-hour show and see what changed
subtitle: Folha de S.Paulo, 2023
description: Fans swap songs into Taylor Swift's Eras Tour setlist and compare how their version's positivity, danceability and energy curve against the original.
solution: Turned a data analysis into something fans could play with. The original setlist stays on screen as a baseline while the edited curve updates, and each bar plays its track.
focus: Built and shipped in a newsroom

title: Run Brazil's election across 27 states
subtitle: Folha de S.Paulo, 2022
description: Two interactive tools that let readers redistribute votes state by state and see the national result change. The second-round version asked where eliminated candidates' voters would go.
solution: Turned state-by-state election results into a tool readers could use on their phones. The same interaction carried into the second round, so the newsroom shipped a second tool on deadline without readers relearning anything.
focus: One pattern reused across two tools

title: Print work
subtitle: Folha de S.Paulo, 2019-2024
description: Graphics for Folha's print edition, from daily charts to full-page features, made across five years at Brazil's largest newspaper. In collaboration with journalist of different desks across the newsroom.
solution: Newspaper stories often turn on data that won't reduce to a single number: several variables moving at once, patterns that only show at full resolution, exceptions that matter as much as the trend. The print graphics kept that density on the page and organised it through hierarchy, annotation and layout, so a reader could take in the headline finding at a glance and then stay to read the detail underneath.
